messages:
Anya: quick sync—need to lock down how sampling decisions propagate through exporters -> retention. leaning tenant-priority first, then per-route head/tail thresholds. thoughts?
Sam: +1 tenant-priority. big customers must have head capture for SLOs. tails can be probabilistic.
Mika: agreed. exporter backpressure is the tricky bit — if exporter queues spike we should escalate drops for tails, keep heads intact.
Jamal: could encode escalation metadata as OTEL attributes, e.g. `redwood.sampling.priority=tenant:2,route:5`, and have sampler honor them.
Lee: doable. console should show effective applied sampling rate per-tenant/route so support can debug. UX: show current policy + historical applied rate and % dropped.
Hannah: rollout note — we need a per-tenant canary toggle for dynamic sampler so SRE can split traffic and auto-rollback on anomalies.
Anya: proposal sketch: 1) attribute-driven priority, 2) exporter-level admission control that signals sampler to escalate tail drops, 3) console surfaces per-tenant retention and canary controls.
Sam: implementation sketch:
```
sampler_config {
  tenant_priority = "int"
  route_weights = { "/login"=10, "/generate"=100 }
  head_rate = 1.0
  base_tail_rate = 0.02
  overload_policy = "escalate_tails"
}
```
Telemetry Bot: config diff applied to staging: sampler_config.overload_policy set to "escalate_tails"
Mika: how do we measure regressions? need an eval set of user flows and per-tenant latency spike detection if sampler misbehaves.
Jamal: add a mirror evaluator: 1% of requests mirror sampling decisions (no-op) and write to a separate retention stream for offline comparison.
Lee: console should surface that mirrored stream and let you query by trace_id -> tenant mapping; also indicate divergence rate between mirrored vs live sampling.
Hannah: can we tie billing/quotas into sampler? i.e., if tenant exceeds token quota, automatically downsample non-critical routes.
Anya: yes, priority order: heads > SLA routes > quota-aware tails. also fallback path: when overloaded, route to lower-cost model variant.
Sam: operational edge: exporter credential rotation or auth failure — sampler must fall back to local strict retention (drop most tails) to avoid unbounded buffering.
Mika: add alerting: if exporter 5xx or auth errors > 5% in 1m, flip to strict retention and page on-call.
Jamal: i'll draft a short RFC with config knobs, console mock screenshots, and rollout plan: canary + mirror + auto-rollback. assigning infra cost estimate to @Sam.
Sam: will estimate delta for mirrored stream + staging canary.
Anya: thanks. Jamal, drop RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
